**Synopsis:**
Chinese government bond (CGB) yields have fallen below 1.7%, diverging sharply from a global sovereign bond sell-off driven by inflation, fiscal stress, and policy credibility concerns. The article explains this divergence is not a sign of Chinese economic strength but rather a structural trap: massive domestic savings (43% of GDP), capital controls preventing capital outflow, deflation, and a lack of safe alternatives (post-property crash, volatile equities) are forcing domestic money into bonds. China's true fiscal picture — when augmented debt including local government vehicles is counted — is worse than headline figures suggest (136% of GDP, rising above 150% by decade-end). HSBC projects the 10-year CGB could fall to 1.50%. The core message: China's low yields reflect trapped liquidity, not fiscal health.
